author: nadgruaz
body:
Hi, 

GO:0016853; F:isomerase activity;  go term to delete 

Human shares 37% amino acid identity with the Arabidopsis enzyme Phzf, which catalyzes hydroxylation of phenazine-1-carboxylic acid to 2-hydroxy-phenazine-1-carboxylic acid.   but not evidence of  catalytic activity in human and co.   in human and mouse , functions as a positive regulator of the antiviral immune response by modulating innate immunity and viral replication.

Many thanks in advance 
Nadine

author: ValWood
body:
For the record, this family is conserved 1:1 across eukaryotes and so its biological role is probably something much more core than  a "regulator of immunity"

At present, it does not have any GO process annotation, that I am aware of. It's one of PomBase's high priority conserved unknowns:

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBPB21E7.07

At SGD the ortholog https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000001071  YHI9
 has a 2006 mutant phenotype annotation to [endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response](https://www.yeastgenome.org/go/GO:0030968)

but a 2020 annotation to chromatin

which seems a bit inconsistent, so I did not transfer these annotations.

TLDR, I don't think we really know the biological role of this protein.

author: ValWood
body:
I don't expect anything to be done with this info, but the human  published role seems odd. This protein seems to have pleiotropic phenotypes across many cancer cell lines (Alliance) and is conserved 1:1 (even in E. coli).
It's very interesting...

author: marcfeuermann
body: I got a look at this family and indeed, from what is known about these proteins, it is not possible to infer the real "core" function for them. I removed the PAINT annotation. Requires probably more evidence to be PAINTed.
